column.text: Bitcoin is sitting just above support at $59,787, and that level decides the next leg. BTC fell 0.83% to $60,062, and the crowded long book makes a break dangerous. The long/short ratio stands at 2.72 with longs at 73.1%, so a clean loss of S1 would force those longs to liquidate into thin bids. Daily RSI at 26.91 shows momentum already stretched to the downside. The divergence is the tell. SPX rose 1.22%, NASDAQ 1.69% and QQQ 1.80%, yet crypto sold off, even with BTC-Nasdaq correlation at 0.72. Crypto failing to follow a rising equity tape is relative weakness, not a dip to buy. Total crypto cap fell 3.40%, stablecoin supply is contracting 5.81% over 30 days, and Fear and Greed reads 12. Flows confirm the bias. BTC ETFs saw −$453.1M on Wednesday 25 Nov and −$3052.1M net over seven days. ETH shed −$68.5M on Wednesday 25 Nov and −$514.9M over the week. SOL was flat on Wednesday at +$0.0M and −$10.4M across seven days. The macro overhang is the Fed. Polymarket prices a 25bp hike at the December meeting at 95%, and the US10Y sits at 4.91%. Dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure has to carry the trade. The regime is risk-off. Favor continuation shorts with momentum. Longs need a real mechanism: deeply negative funding, a capitulation reading, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown at S1. Anything else is a bounce to sell. A daily close below $58,525 would confirm the broader downtrend, and until then the shorts have the tape.
